overview: Bharatmala Pariyojana is a flagship infrastructure initiative by the Government of India aimed at improving road connectivity across the country, particularly in border areas, coastal regions, and economic corridors. It focuses on developing National Highways, strategic roads, and interconnecting routes to enhance regional integration and support economic growth. The scheme is implemented by agencies like NHIDCL under the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways, with projects spanning multiple states and union territories.
objectives: Develop approximately 24,800 km of roads under Phase-I
Improve connectivity in border, coastal, and tribal areas
Enhance efficiency of national corridors through multi-modal integration
Support economic corridors and feeder routes
Strengthen infrastructure in the North Eastern Region and strategic areas
Facilitate seamless movement of goods and passenger traffic
Promote sustainable and environmentally conscious highway development
Boost regional development and inclusive growth
eligibility: The scheme is implemented by government agencies and public sector undertakings like NHIDCL under the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways. Projects are sanctioned based on technical feasibility, strategic importance, and alignment with national infrastructure priorities. Eligibility for funding and execution is determined by the government through appraisal and approval processes.
benefits: Improved road connectivity leading to reduced logistics costs and travel time; enhanced access to remote and underdeveloped regions; boost to trade, commerce, and industrial activity; better access to healthcare, education, and markets; strengthened national security through border road development; employment generation during construction and maintenance; promotion of regional integration and economic corridors.
financial_support: Financial support for Bharatmala Pariyojana is provided through central government budgetary allocations, market borrowings, and private investment via public-private partnerships (PPP). NHIDCL executes projects using government funding and has accessed external financing from institutions like the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) for specific high-speed corridor projects.
application_process: 1. Project identification and feasibility studies conducted by NHIDCL or other implementing agencies. 2. Preparation of Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) including technical, economic, and environmental assessments. 3. Submission of DPRs to the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways for appraisal and approval. 4. Sanction of projects based on priority and availability of funds. 5. Tendering process for selection of contractors through competitive bidding. 6. Award of contracts and commencement of civil works. 7. Monitoring and supervision during construction. 8. Commissioning and handover for operation and maintenance.
deadlines: Rolling basis — projects are sanctioned and implemented based on annual planning and budget cycles.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Road Transport & Highways, Government of India
contact_details: Email: cvo[dot]nhidcl-morth[at]gov[dot]in | Chief Vigilance Officer: Ashish Nath
caveats: Project timelines may vary due to land acquisition, environmental clearances, and geographical challenges
Funding is subject to annual budget allocations and parliamentary approvals
PPP models depend on private sector participation and viability gap funding
Completion targets are indicative and may be revised based on field conditions
